answer: Node2vec does not use spectral clustering to build its embeddings, so the question's premise is incorrect. Node2vec generates embeddings by running second-order biased random walks over the graph, controlled by return (p) and in-out (q) parameters that interpolate between breadth-first and depth-first exploration. It then feeds these walks as sequences into the skip-gram model with negative sampling (the word2vec objective) to learn node representations. Spectral methods such as Laplacian eigenmaps or matrix factorization appear in the node2vec paper only as related-work baselines and comparison points. The Wikipedia dataset in the node2vec paper is a word co-occurrence network in which nodes are words and labels are part-of-speech tags. It is used to evaluate the learned embeddings on multi-label node classification, not to illustrate spectral clustering.
confidence_reasoning: I am confident node2vec uses biased random walks with skip-gram rather than spectral clustering and that the Wikipedia dataset is a POS-tag co-occurrence network, though I am less certain of the exact baselines and details of the dataset description.
